purpose: Give an exact accepted standalone Plan one durable Hosted Redirect dispatch claim for local TEST proof.

implementation_revision.semantics: E1a-F dispatch foundation with WELL-219 known-reference scheduling on the existing claim.

collaborating_domains.ownership: Current verified canonical account and active session. Commerce checks the accepted payer relationship.
TEST suppression status for both accepted parties. Commerce reuses the S1 Privacy locks.

ash.caller_boundary: Private actions and deny-all policies. The owning interface checks current payer, exact source and fixed fixture scope.
S1 owns acceptance. HostedCheckout locks and reads the original Purchase without writing accepted values.

side_effects: Bind one random reference and a digest of the accepted snapshot.
caller_constraints: TEST only. Requires the current payer, allowed Privacy scopes and an unpaid standalone Plan.

arguments: Isolated loopback listener port, with an exact DER certificate for Verify-enabled claims
returns: Retained or ambiguous outcome, or scoped denial.
side_effects: Commit the sole claim, prove it is visible independently and perform at most one loopback POST. Retain a matching fixture capability.
caller_constraints: TEST only. Requires the original prepared binding and an outermost commit boundary.

returns: Original reference and its prepared, retained or ambiguous status, or scoped denial.
side_effects: Read the current dispatch outcome and apply existing Identity session checks without HTTP.
caller_constraints: TEST only. Requires the current payer and unchanged source.

request_flow.summary: Lock the Purchase, revalidate actor and Privacy authority, rebuild S1's accepted snapshot and reject a paid or changed source.
Bind the reference to the existing Purchase.attempt_id. Commit the claim in a separate transaction and read the exact epoch and reference through an unboxed PostgreSQL connection before sending.
Only the claim winner enters the fixed Req path. Retain the matching code under the same claim and check payer authority again before returning the capability.

side_effects: Persist a stable reference and accepted snapshot digest.
Commit the only claim ID. Failed or uncertain acknowledgements leave the claim intact.
WELL-219 binds the local Verify listener and persists the first due time with the claim.

guards: Canonical non-routable fixture URL and code
side_effects: Retain the fixture code once. The current payer can recover the original URL.

security_invariants.summary: The recipient may observe the S1 purchase and still lack initiation and capability recovery authority. Current canonical payer and Privacy checks apply at both boundaries.

The wire code compiles only in TEST. It accepts no host, credential, proxy, plugin or middleware override. The numeric loopback host, fixture credential and synthetic contact are fixed. Verify-enabled claims require TLS authenticated to the exact listener certificate.
Publish only response classifications and timings. Mark reference and code sensitive and hide both from ordinary outcome inspection.

A bound local attempt cannot accept synthetic P1/S1 payment evidence. A separate unbound S1 fixture still accepts qualified synthetic observations. No local dispatch releases the Assessment interlock or creates rights.

concurrency.summary: The Purchase lock serializes dispatch admission and the existing synthetic application path. Private claim and retention updates filter on the unconsumed or matching epoch respectively.

The action rejects explicit outer transactions and reads the exact claim from a different unboxed connection. This also excludes an implicit SQL Sandbox savepoint. The receiver counts actual POSTs independently.

idempotency_retry.summary: Exact replay recovers the original reference. A committed claim remains consumed after a lost response, timeout, error envelope or application restart.
Req uses HTTP/1, disables retries and redirects, bounds pool/connect/receive and best-effort exchange times, and caps the response body at 16 KiB.

failure_recovery.summary: Pre-commit rollback preserves the original prepared reference for its first dispatch. After commitment the claim is ambiguous until applicable evidence is retained, even when the receiver saw no request.
An exact fixture capability commits before presentation. A fresh BEAM reloads the original result after a lost response or interrupted presentation without another send.
The additive schema leaves P1, S1 and E2a rows intact. Rollback holds an exclusive table lock and refuses to erase a retained binding.

cases: F-01/F-02 exact snapshot, actor and authority denials
tests.proves: Exact accepted money, wrong source and scope denial, revoked and suppressed actor denial, quote-less and closed exclusions, zero local payments and rights, and preserved admission interlock.
tests.limits: Signed synthetic P1, S1 and E2a inputs remain TEST fixtures.

cases: F-03 separate PostgreSQL connections and committed request count
F-04/F-05 rollback, lost response, restart and fail-closed replay
tests.proves: Actual lock wait, no wire request before visibility, one receiver request across a race, exact original reference across four cuts, and no disclosure after revocation.

cases: F-06/F-07 exact response, non-retry, no redirects, redaction
tests.proves: Fixed endpoint and settings despite poison defaults, separate attempt and wire counts, bounded response size and timeout, and sanitized diagnostics.
tests.limits: Local wire evidence earns no provider-stage certification.

cases: F-10 additive migration and protected rollback
tests.proves: Up/down/up with legacy rows, local foreign key, scoped unique index and scope, binding and capability shape checks.
tests.limits: Real DDL in a rollback-isolated schema.

cases: F-07 compile exclusion and runtime configuration denial
tests.proves: The non-TEST BEAM has no wire builder or Ash/Req imports in the owner boundary. Public calls remain disabled.
tests.limits: Uses compiled modules without starting the application. The existing runner contract checks that both standalone WELL-218 proof scripts stay out of ExUnit discovery.

safe_extensions.summary: WELL-190 owns any future external activation. Reverify the actual stack and qualify exact provider evidence before changing the fixture isolation or replacement rules.

reuse.summary: EXTEND the PR #312 matrix with the reviewed draft Store PR #234 head cdb56c61137bd27d4c13bcb66941611792b2b5f5. Adapt checkout_payload and request in lib/store/payments/providers/paystack.ex, the checkout envelope from lib/store/payments/providers/paystack/response.ex, non-idempotent request settings from lib/store/support/http/req_client.ex, and exact-payload and reference-mismatch cases from test/store/payments/providers/paystack_checkout_test.exs. NewYou uses the locked Req 0.7.5 stack and an actual Bandit loopback receiver.

COMPOSE Store main 949821ac589addb6e595f6333370ed65cf8d5ef7, lib/store/subscriptions/renewal_collection_attempts.ex, claim_dispatch_locked, ensure_exact_dispatch_epoch and claim_collection_dispatch. Use Commerce-owned filtered Ash actions, the existing Purchase lock and one immutable claim epoch.

prohibited_shortcuts.summary: Exclude missing-reference replay, overlapping sends, stale setup cancellation and imported Store business Domains. Initialize evidence alone cannot authorize replacement, cancellation, payment or entitlement.

proof_limitations: HIGH proof covers binding, actor authority, request and durable-effect counts, recovery, redaction and migration. Provider reconciliation, browser rendering, financial settlement, entitlement application and release remain separate.
Only a validated code for a reserved non-routable fixture origin is retained. Real provider capabilities, credentials, HTTPS policy and empirical verdicts belong to WELL-190.
Standalone Plan has no new unpaid terminality rule. Existing paid or corrected sources remain ineligible. All Assessment and bundle dispatch stays disabled.
